title: Recall aloud before the options appear
statement: In a retrieval warm-up, have learners answer aloud before any options appear, and show the options only afterwards as a check, so they recall rather than recognise.
detail: A review of a Grade 3 reading build welcomed starting with retrieval from the last lesson but said it would be better done with an oral response than a multiple-choice question; the redesign brief records the defect, that the warm-up was a choice question, so the child recognised instead of retrieving. The rebuilt warm-up asks its question alone and the child answers out loud, and only on the next screen do the options appear, under a heading telling the child to check, with a written response for each choice. The build's principle is that the child speaks before they choose.
